overall_conclusion: F1/F2 source defects and a flag-dependent mapped-buffer/AIO cleanup defect are real findings in this published 4.19.124 source. No demonstrated real-device USB-host arbitrary physical read/write, attacker-selected AIO free, decrypted rootfs export, firmware decoder or proprietary memory consumer is established. Document overstates S5 absence, model transfer and JTAG exclusivity.

findings.analysis: Both asynchronous iter paths allocate zeroed ffs_io_data and neither assigns p->buf from the iovec before ffs_epfile_io. The physical-address branch consequently consumes zero, rather than a USB-host-selected or iovec-selected physical address. io_data->buf is later replaced by the translated data pointer and completion frees it. A conditional invalid-free defect is supported, but the arbitrary-address/free-list/code-execution claims require additional, currently absent, consumers or memory-corruption evidence.

findings.analysis: Checked endpoint file operations register read_iter/write_iter, whose zeroed ffs_io_data.buf is not initialized from the iterator. Helpers that actually assign the supplied buffer address have aio=false and are reached through local FUNCTIONFS_IO_READ/WRITE ioctls. Merely writing the physical value as the buffer argument of ordinary read/write or io_submit does not establish the claimed address selection in this tree. This audit supplies no exploitation procedure.

findings.claim: A USB trace can directly establish FunctionFS physical-address flag or AIO use

evidence.path: <USER_DESKTOP>/FunctionFS漏洞链路复核与S5迁移性结论_20261013.md

findings.analysis: The FunctionFS v2 magic/length/flags header is written by local userspace to ep0 and parsed into ffs->user_flags; it is not the USB on-wire configuration-descriptor header. AIO selection is determined by local kiocb state. usbmon/Wireshark records USB traffic, and cannot directly disclose this local descriptor header, I/O syscall selection or buffer-pointer provenance. ELF-like or arbitrary returned bytes also do not prove flags, physical address origin, or a new image consumer.

findings.claim: Crash at translated physical address proves successful physical-memory readback

evidence.path: <USER_DESKTOP>/FunctionFS漏洞链路复核与S5迁移性结论_20261013.md

findings.analysis: Completion computes ret from req->status or actual. It performs read-copy only for positive ret, but kfree(io_data->buf) is unconditional after completion; an I/O error can therefore still lead to invalid free/crash. A register or crash address establishes neither successful USB bytes nor contents, length, provenance, or rootfs identity.

findings.claim: F1/F2 array bounds defects exist in the supplied 4.19.124 source

evidence.path: <USER_DESKTOP>/FunctionFS漏洞链路复核与S5迁移性结论_20261013.md

findings.analysis: Dispatcher checks the low byte yet passes full wIndex to FunctionFS. Reverse mapping narrows interface to u8 while subsequent array indexing uses original unsigned interface. Source supports out-of-bounds read/write conditions. Writes occur only after active-state and endpoint-enable return checks; reads with a negative int value produce no response data in composite. Host-visible readback is at most one byte per successful request, while writes affect a bounded array-relative location, not an arbitrary physical pointer. A running configured FunctionFS target and matching compiled code remain unverified.

findings.analysis: The code conditionally translates a pointer or maps it according to local descriptor flags, queues it as endpoint transfer buffer, and exposes local ioctl helpers. No supplied proprietary daemon implementation establishes that a USB/PTP parameter controls flags, local ioctl choice, physical pointer and length. Valid mapping, UDC/DMA behavior, active endpoint and transfer completion are additional requirements. Kernel source capability is not a validated memory-dump command.
